style: Say casually and naturally, like a friendly teenager explaining a puzzle.
lines: Pick an equation from the menu. Then tap plus or minus under a substance and watch the atom ledger.
Balance each equation in the smallest whole numbers. Tap plus or minus under a substance to add molecules.
Pick a card from the list. Examples come solved; on the others, tap the product you think forms.
Change the subscript and you change the substance. Tap Put it back.
Odd oxygen? Tap plus under the fuel to double it first.
Balanced. Same atoms, same mass, both sides.
That balances, but you can divide every number down.
Tap plus or minus under a substance, or type its count. Compare the two sides of the atom ledger.
Use the group charges above the trays. Tap the product formula whose charges cancel.
Sodium in water is a teacher demo behind a shield. Pick P9 from the list to try the same pattern.
This example is already balanced. Pick the next card from the list to try the same pattern.
Those charges do not cancel for the product in this pattern. Read the charge explanation, then choose again.
The product fits this pattern. Now use the coefficient boxes to balance the atoms.
Start with the element that is in only one substance on each side. Tap its substance count to adjust it.
Leave elements that appear alone, like oxygen gas, for last. Adjust the other substances first.
Find a row that does not match. Add whole molecules on the short side with the plus button.
This group breaks apart here. Keep counting individual atoms in the ledger.
Count intact groups as units. Change coefficients and compare the group row in the ledger.
All counts are one again. Tap plus or minus to adjust the whole molecules.
Every substance in the equation has to be there at least once. Enter an integer from one to thirty.
Progress cleared on this device. Choose an equation to balance.
